items.note: Part of one status vocabulary across the library: `error` is the word every component uses now.

items.action: Rename `[danger]` to `[error]` on ds-modal-card.

Replace `variant="danger"` with `variant="error"` on ds-stat.
items.appliesWhen: Other variant values are unchanged and absent from the map — leave them.
items.note: Part of one status vocabulary across the library: every component says error where some used to say danger.
items.verify: No ds-stat binds variant="danger". Every stat that used to be danger renders in the error colour, and stats on other variant values are untouched.

items.action: Rename `variant="warn"` to `variant="warning"`, and move `variant="indeterminate"` to the bare `indeterminate` attribute. Update TS references to the removed `ProgressVariant` members; the union is `default | success | warning | error` now.
items.appliesWhen: success, error and default are unchanged and absent from the map.
items.pitfall: `indeterminate` was a variant VALUE and is a boolean input now, so the two are no longer mutually exclusive — a bar can be success-coloured and indeterminate at once. Leaving `variant="indeterminate"` in place gives an unknown value, which resolves to the default colour and a determinate bar.
items.note: Two axes were conflated in one input. Colour and progress state are independent, so the state moved out to its own boolean and the colour vocabulary joined the library-wide status words.
items.verify: No ds-progress binds `variant="warn"` or `variant="indeterminate"`: the colour vocabulary is `default | success | warning | error`, and the indeterminate state is the bare `indeterminate` attribute. Nothing is typed with a removed ProgressVariant member.

items.action: Three coupled steps. (1) Rename the input, keeping the value: `variant="active"` → `status="active"`, `[variant]="expr"` → `[status]="expr"`. Exception: `variant="solid"` becomes the bare `solid` attribute and `variant="count"` becomes `[count]="n"` with the number moved out of the content - they were a fill and a shape, not statuses. (2) Wire the colours through the `styles/status` SCSS API keyed on `[data-status]` — see status-lifecycle-tokens-removed for the snippet. (3) Augment DsStatusRegistry with your keys so DsStatusKey narrows from an open string to your union. Full guide: migrations/0.5.1/badge-statuses.md.
items.appliesWhen: `[count]`, `[solid]`, `[withDot]`, `[max]` and every `--ds-badge-*` hook are unchanged. If you coloured badges through your OWN class (`class="chip {{ status }}"`), that keeps working — but any value that used to fall through to a factory colour is now uncoloured.
items.pitfall: Step 1 alone leaves every badge UNCOLOURED, because the component ships no built-in colour for any value. And a static `variant="x"` left behind fails silently: Angular ignores an unknown attribute instead of erroring, so the badge renders plain with nothing in the console. Grep `variant=` scoped to ds-badge.
items.note: The value is emitted as a `data-status` attribute now rather than a status-named CSS class, and the input is typed DsStatusKey.
items.verify: No `variant` remains on the component. The chips render in their status colours, not grey: the `styles/status` partial is included and any custom status is registered through DsStatusRegistry, or the colour resolves to the neutral default and you meant that.

items.action: Switch any CSS targeting `.status-dot.active`, `.planning`, `.confirmed`, `.completed`, `.warning`, `.error` or `.secondary` to `[data-status='…']`, and define the colours through the `styles/status` SCSS API.
items.pitfall: The input name did not change, so a search for `status` finds nothing wrong while the class-based CSS stops matching. It also no longer defaults to `planning` — a dot with no status now has none.
items.note: `[status]` is retyped from StatusValue to DsStatusKey and the value reaches the DOM as `data-status`.
items.verify: No CSS targets `.status-dot.<value>` (the value is a data-status attribute now) and nothing types a status with StatusValue instead of DsStatusKey.
items.restore: status="planning" stated explicitly, where a dot relied on the old default

items.action: Type badge and status-dot status with DsStatusKey, or with your own union registered through a DsStatusRegistry augmentation.
items.note: BadgeVariant, BadgeLifecycle, BadgeSemantic and StatusValue are no longer exported.
items.verify: None of the four removed type names is imported; badge and status-dot statuses are typed DsStatusKey or a registry-augmented union.

items.action: Declare your statuses through the styles/status API instead: `@use '@ids-group-ltd/ids-design-system/styles/status' as status;` then `@include status.define(('completed': (bg: var(--success), text: var(--text-on-success)), 'active': (bg: var(--info-subtitle), text: var(--info-text))));` — one entry per value you pass to `[status]`, shape `(bg required, text?, dot?)`. `status.semantic-preset` covers the info/success/warning/error/neutral set. Pair it with the DsStatusRegistry augmentation. Full guide: migrations/0.5.1/badge-statuses.md.
items.appliesWhen: The dimension token `--status-dot-size` is NOT removed and needs nothing.
items.pitfall: These tokens were the only colour the lifecycle badges had (status-dot used its own fallbacks, also gone). Without replacements the elements render with no status colour - nothing errors.
items.note: The factory lifecycle tokens `--status-planning-*`, `--status-confirmed-*`, `--status-active-*` and `--status-completed-*` are gone; the API writes the public `--ds-badge-*` / `--ds-status-dot-*` hooks keyed on `[data-status]`.
items.verify: No stylesheet declares a --status-<lifecycle>-* token; a themed lifecycle status is declared through the styles/status Sass API instead.

items.action: Look at anything using the secondary or tertiary roles. To keep the old single-hue look, set `--secondary-h/s/l` and `--tertiary-h/s/l` back to `var(--primary-h/s/l)`.
items.appliesWhen: Only if you never set those channels yourself. If you did, your values still win.
items.pitfall: Both roles used to fall through to the primary channels, so everything that read them was blue. They are orange and violet now, and because no markup or API moved, the only thing that reports it is a screen.
items.note: `--secondary-h/s/l` default to the `--orange` family and `--tertiary-h/s/l` to `--violet`.
items.restore: --secondary-h/s/l and --tertiary-h/s/l pointed back at the --primary channels
items.verify: An app that never set those channels has looked at every secondary and tertiary surface (they are orange and violet now, not blue), or pins them back.

items.action: Replace `var(--static-white)` with the keyword `white`.
items.note: Identical value, no visual change — the fixed-value custom property earned nothing over the keyword.
items.verify: No stylesheet reads var(--static-white); the literal `white` stands in its place.

items.action: Build after upgrading, then rename your own member or mark it `override` wherever the compiler reports a collision with a class in `detect`. Delete an override of a member the class lost.
items.appliesWhen: Only a class that extends one of the classes in `detect`. A consumer who uses the elements in templates needs nothing from this item.
items.pitfall: `private` and `protected` give no protection: a member you redeclare collides with a base member of any visibility. A member of yours that replaced a lost one no longer replaces anything, and the component stops calling it.
items.note: Most of these are the input and output renames above, seen from a subclass. `AlertComponent`, `BannerComponent` and `ToastComponent` each gained `closed` and lost `dismissed`. `AutocompleteComponent`, `MultiSelectComponent`, `PopoverComponent` and `TimePickerComponent` each gained `host` and `panelTokens`. `BadgeComponent` gained `status` and lost `variant`. `ColorPickerComponent` gained `panelTokens`. `DatePickerComponent` gained `ghostRemainder`, `host` and `panelTokens`. `MenuItemComponent`, `ModalCardComponent` and `ModalComponent` each gained `error` and lost `danger`. `ProgressComponent` gained `indeterminate`. `SplitButtonComponent` gained `itemSelected` and lost `itemSelect`. `StatusDotComponent` lost `classes`. `StepperComponent` gained `stepClicked` and lost `stepClick`. `TableComponent` gained `rowClicked` and lost `rowClick`. `TabsComponent` gained `tabClosed` and lost `tabClose`. `TreeComponent` gained `nodeSelected` and lost `nodeSelect`.
items.verify: The app builds with no error naming a class listed in `detect`, and every member of such a subclass that shares a base member's name is marked `override`.

informational: New extensible status system: DsStatusRegistry / DsStatusKey type exports + styles/status SCSS API (define($map) / semantic-preset) — the additive half of the badge/status-dot status redesign.
Additive: DsStatus type export ('info'|'success'|'warning'|'error'); ds-progress [indeterminate] boolean input; DividerSpacing now re-exported from the public API.

Visual/behavioral only, no code change: press-feedback reworked (no button-style press on non-buttons; list/menu rows and color-picker trigger get a flat :active tint; small icon action buttons — close/dismiss/clear/remove x and the ds-tag chip close — get the button press-scale); booleanAttribute coercion on ~54 boolean inputs; ds-button tonal :active now darkens past hover (`--ds-button-bg-color-active` on `variant="tonal"` defaults to the hover tint mixed 10% toward black, was the hover tint itself; restore with e.g. `--ds-button-bg-color-active: var(--primary-muted-strong)` on primary tonal buttons).

Fixes, no action required: overlay panel --ds-* overrides now reach the portaled pane (ds-autocomplete/ds-multi-select/ds-date-picker/ds-color-picker/ds-popover/ds-time-picker); ds-autocomplete/ds-multi-select panels no longer render transparent; ds-tabs secondary variant now applies; ds-date-picker range mask no longer clips the second date + tighter value-to-icon gap; the ultra-compact density tier now scales avatar/sidenav/badge/status-dot/switch geometry (its switch: `--switch-track-h` 14px, `--switch-thumb-size` 10px, `--switch-thumb-travel` 10px, were 20px, 12px, 16px; the rest: `--avatar-md` 20px, `--badge-dot-size` 4px, `--status-dot-size` 5px, `--sidenav-w` 200px, `--field-floating-label-top` 4px, were the root 32px, 6px, 8px, 240px, 8px; set them back under `[data-density="ultra-compact"]` to restore).

Visual/behavioral only, no code change: ds-date-picker keeps the format mask visible while typing — the unfilled tail of the mask stays on-screen as a muted ghost (e.g. "12/DD/YYYY") and the typed value renders in the monospace font for exact glyph alignment.
